qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Global pioneer in offshore wind development. The economic engine was devastated by severe cost inflation, installation vessel bottlenecks, turbine supply delays, and soaring interest rates that struck fixed-bid auction power contracts lacking inflation indexation. The inability to pass through cost increases resulted in over DKK 40B in cumulative impairments and project cancellations (notably Ocean Wind 1 in the US), forcing dividend suspensions and asset disposals. Reported multi-cycle ROCE collapsed to -14.2% in 2023 and only recovered to 4.5%-5.4% in 2024-2025, completely failing the 12% ROIC and pricing power >= inflation hurdles.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (Proof of Moat & Pricing Power, REJECT). Offshore wind pioneer exposed to catastrophic project delivery risks. Fixed-price power purchase and auction contracts demonstrated zero pricing power when turbine, vessel, and capital costs spiked, resulting in DKK 26.8B+ in write-downs in 2023, US project abandonments, and dividend cancellation. Multi-cycle ROCE (-14% in 2023, ~5% in 2024-2025) fails the 12% threshold.
qualitative.evidence: In FY2023, Ørsted posted an impairment charge of DKK 26.8B primarily from stopping development on US Ocean Wind 1, driving reported ROCE to -14.2%. Even adjusted ROCE fell from 12.9% in 2023 to 10.1% in 2024 and 8.4% in 2025, while reported ROCE was 4.5% (2024) and 5.4% (2025). Net interest-bearing debt expanded to DKK 58B in 2024 before asset sales and rights issue restructuring reduced it in 2025. The core business lacks pricing power against construction and financing inflation.
